title: Friday, November 13
script:
Good morning. Today is Friday, November thirteenth, twenty twenty-six.

It is a sunny day in Arkadelphia with a high near fifty-eight degrees and zero percent chance of rain. A freeze warning is currently active across the region. Expect widespread frost to develop tonight after ten p.m. under mostly clear skies as the temperature drops to a low around twenty-nine degrees. Frost will remain widespread on Saturday morning before nine a.m., followed by mostly sunny skies and a high near fifty-five degrees. Sunrise was at six forty-three a.m., and sunset will be at five zero nine p.m.

Turning to the top national and world headlines.

Per NPR, Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang has stepped down following personal scandals and growing political fallout. The tech company's chief financial officer has been appointed interim chief executive officer to navigate a legal mess, ongoing supply chain concerns, and foreign export scrutiny. BBC reports that Democratic lawmakers and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have raised questions over Commerce Department oversight regarding chip exports linked to China.

In Washington politics, Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. Van Hollen, who serves as the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee, stated that new leadership is needed following recent midterm election results.

In international sports, United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is leaving his post. Pochettino, who led the United States to the round of sixteen at the last World Cup, has been named the new manager of Manchester United.

Meanwhile, Microsoft is working to fully restore services following a massive global tech outage. The disruption affected Outlook email, Teams videoconferencing, and Copilot software, causing delays for airlines, government offices, and businesses worldwide.

Moving over to the N-F-L and the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Kansas City Chiefs are standing by placekicker Harrison Butker despite his ongoing slump. Head coach Andy Reid and special teams coordinator Dave Toub confirmed this week that Butker will remain the starter for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Butker has missed seven of his nineteen field goal attempts this season, converting just over sixty-three percent of his kicks.

As Kansas City prepares for Atlanta, the Chiefs defense is focused on stopping Falcons running back Bijan Robinson, who currently leads the league in rushing yards. Robinson barely edges out Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker, who has accumulated eight hundred seventy-two yards on the year. On the Chiefs injury front, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods missed his second straight practice Thursday with a neck injury, while starting right tackle Jaylon Moore sat out with an ankle issue. Additionally, former starting punt returner Nikko Remigio posted a goodbye message to fans after signing with the Houston Texans active roster.

Across the league, teams are evaluating their rosters following Tuesday's trade deadline as division races heat up for the second half of the season.

Next up, Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball.

The Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team continues to build momentum early in the season following a key win against Kentucky. Head coach Bill Self publicly detailed how the Jayhawks successfully neutralized Kentucky's top three-point shooter during their matchup. Highly touted freshman Tyran Stokes has also drawn attention after working on his game with former N-B-A veteran Jamal Crawford, as the coaching staff works through early-season free throw performance.

Let's check in on fantasy football.

Major injury updates are shaking up fantasy lineups for Week Ten. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been placed on injured reserve after suffering M-C-L and P-C-L sprains along with turf toe. Meanwhile, New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson is expected to clear concussion protocol and suit up against the Buffalo Bills.

For running backs, Cam Skattebo is taking over primary duties in the New York Giants backfield, making him a top player to target on waivers. New England Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson returned to practice in Munich despite a knee issue, while fantasy managers should monitor Cincinnati's Corey Kiner and Denver's Audric Estime for potential breakout touches.

Taking a look at the weather out in Los Angeles.

Los Angeles is facing a wet Friday with rain, showers, and thunderstorms likely before four p.m. High temperatures will reach around seventy-two degrees under mostly cloudy skies, with an eighty-five percent chance of rain and rainfall totals up to half an inch. Showers will linger into tonight before four a.m., with a low near fifty-seven degrees and wind gusts reaching twenty miles per hour. Sunny skies return on Saturday with a high near seventy-two degrees. Sunrise was at six twenty-four a.m., and sunset is at four fifty p.m.

Heading into entertainment and screenwriting news.

Deadline reports that Paramount's new holiday horror film Ebenezer pulled in one point five million dollars in Thursday preview screenings. Directed by Ti West, the P-G-thirteen dark take on A Christmas Carol is aiming for a forty million dollar worldwide opening weekend as Johnny Depp returns to the box office.

Country music legend Dolly Parton's final recorded vocal performance was released today. The track is a duet with U-Two on their single Torn, included on the band's new album Carnaval de Luz. In music television news, The Hollywood Reporter confirms that Taylor Swift is set to perform live at the C-M-A Awards for the first time in thirteen years.

In legal news, London's Metropolitan Police have launched an investigation into comedian David Walliams regarding allegations of serious historical sexual offenses. Meanwhile, a new documentary examining disgraced comedian Russell Brand has premiered as he faces further misconduct allegations while serving a ten-year prison sentence.

Turning to artificial intelligence and tech news.

TechCrunch reports that Google officially launched its new Gemini four Hydrogen artificial intelligence model today. Powered by enhanced reasoning capabilities, the new model is designed to handle complex, multi-part questions and is now rolling out across Google Search, the Gemini app, and developer A-P-Is.

OpenAI released ChatGPT Wallet for U.S. Pro subscribers, enabling artificial intelligence agents to research products and complete online checkouts automatically on behalf of users. Additionally, ElevenLabs launched ElevenAI, a new app that combines meeting transcription and dictation tools tailored for business teams.

Down in Brazil, here is the weather for Rio de Janeiro.

Rio de Janeiro is experiencing light drizzle today with a high near eighty-four degrees and a low around seventy-two degrees. Rain chances are high at ninety-four percent, with wind gusts reaching up to twenty-four miles per hour. Sunrise was at five zero one a.m., and sunset will be at six twelve p.m. local time.

Finally, national and local news out of Brazil.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva arrived in Manila today for an official state visit to the Philippines before attending the forty-ninth A-S-E-A-N Summit. Back home, Brazil's industrial confidence index dropped six points to forty point two in November, hitting its lowest level since May twenty twenty.

In local Rio de Janeiro news, eighty-four-year-old actress Neusa Borges has been admitted to a hospital in Copacabana. Meanwhile, state officials have accelerated their summer emergency plan to handle weather impacts from El Nino, as Rio's famous floating Christmas tree at Lagoa marks its thirtieth anniversary.

That's the paper.

title: Thursday, November 12
script:
Good morning, it is Thursday, November twelfth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, you are looking at a sunny day with a high near sixty-nine degrees, though temperatures will dip toward sixty-five this afternoon. Expect north-northwest winds around five miles per hour with gusts reaching twenty. Tonight, skies will be mostly clear with a low around thirty-three degrees, and a frost advisory is in effect. You can expect widespread frost before eight a.m. tomorrow, followed by a sunny Friday with a high near fifty-nine, with temperatures falling to around fifty-five in the afternoon. Sunrise was at six forty-two a.m. and sunset is at five oh nine p.m.

Moving to the top headlines, a tragic shooting occurred at a gym in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle Thursday morning. Police confirmed that one person was killed and four others were injured, and the gunman is now dead. On the international stage, U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin to discuss the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The pair is scheduled to fly to Ireland later today for follow-up talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Meanwhile, the massive ocean liner SS United States is being sunk off the coast of Florida to be transformed into an artificial reef. In political news, Democrat Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate race, becoming the first Black senator in the state since eighteen seventy-four. The White House has also issued a warning to Democrats who are planning to launch investigations into the administration. Additionally, the vice president of Indonesia has resigned following questions regarding his academic credentials and eligibility, and in Italy, a second day of bomb hoax threats has forced fresh evacuations of schools across the country.

In the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs are moving forward after acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a pair of Day three draft selections. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes says he does not expect a long learning period for his new target and believes it is realistic for Downs to see the field quickly. On the injury front, the team’s Wednesday report showed defensive tackle Peter Woods missing practice with a neck injury, while starting right tackle Jaylon Moore also sat out with an ankle issue. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed he is sticking with veteran kicker Harrison Butker for this week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons despite a recent string of missed field goals. Defensive tackle Chris Jones has been named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his two-sack performance against the New York Jets. Off the field, the Chiefs have named HNTB as their official architect for stadium planning.

For Kansas men’s basketball, the Jayhawks are riding high following a dominant win over Kentucky in the Champions Classic in Chicago. The team’s deep roster and offensive firepower were on full display, with Trey Kaufman-Renn highlighted as a player making a significant difference for the squad.

Looking at fantasy football, the trade of Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs has made him a priority waiver wire pickup for managers looking for depth. With Puka Nacua dealing with an injury, Konata Mumpfield is emerging as a potential sleeper option to fill the gap. Managers should also be aware that Kewan Lacy is out for the season, and there are ongoing injury updates for players like George Pickens and A.J. Brown. For tonight’s game between the Commanders and the Giants, fantasy owners should monitor the status of running back Cam Skattebo.

In Los Angeles, today will be sunny with a high near eighty-one degrees. Rain showers are likely tonight after ten p.m., with a sixty percent chance of precipitation and a low around fifty-nine. Friday will see rain showers and potential thunderstorms before the afternoon, with a high near seventy-four. An air quality alert is currently active. Sunrise was at six twenty-three a.m. and sunset is at four fifty p.m.

In Hollywood, Brad Pitt is set to star in a new feature titled Connector, which will be produced by his banner, Plan B, for Apple. Paramount+ has greenlit a new sports comedy series titled Day One’s, featuring Damian Lewis and produced by Matthew Vaughn, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Thierry Henry. In other screenwriting and production news, Teyonah Parris and Danielle Brooks are set to star in a new Peacock series titled Before I Let Go, based on the novel by Kennedy Ryan. Lucasfilm has announced that the original nineteen seventy-seven Star Wars will be re-released in IMAX seventy-millimeter as part of the franchise’s fiftieth anniversary celebrations next year. Meanwhile, the documentary film You Can See Everything, about Elizabeth Holmes, has tied with American Doctor for the most nominations in this year's Cinema Eye Honors.

In the world of technology, the industry is reeling from the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The board accepted his resignation after reports surfaced regarding extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed as the interim CEO, and Huang has agreed to testify before Congress. In other tech news, a study by the IP protection firm Podqi found that AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are sometimes recommending fake retail websites to shoppers. Additionally, game developers are increasingly turning to generative AI, with forty percent of those surveyed in a recent industry report saying they use the tools as part of their daily work.

Finally, in Brazil, the federal police have opened an inquiry into United States funding for the political campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro. In the business sector, Conasa has won a highway concession auction worth two point eight billion dollars. In Rio de Janeiro, health officials at Fiocruz are reporting a rise in severe COVID-19 cases, specifically those involving acute respiratory syndrome. On a lighter note, the city has opened its first baby park in the Tijuca neighborhood, featuring play equipment for children under the age of three. Weather in Rio today is overcast with a high near eighty-three degrees and a low around sixty-nine. Sunrise was at five oh two a.m. and sunset is at six eleven p.m.

That's the paper.

title: Wednesday, November 11
script:
Good morning. Today is Wednesday, November eleventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with your local weather in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies for Veterans Day with a high near seventy-nine degrees, though temperatures will dip to around seventy-five in the afternoon. Winds will come out of the west at five to ten miles per hour, bringing gusts up to twenty miles per hour, and there is only a two percent chance of rain. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around forty-four degrees and light northwest winds. Thursday stays sunny with a high near seventy degrees, cooling to around sixty-five in the afternoon. Sunrise is at six forty-one a.m. and sunset is at five ten p.m.

Moving into national and world news, Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a major prisoner of war exchange following United States mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. According to reports from NPR and the BBC, this represents the largest humanitarian release since the conflict began in twenty twenty-two. While the negotiators discussed Europe's broader post-war security framework, the meetings concluded without a major diplomatic breakthrough.

Meanwhile, federal prosecutors have charged three alleged Iran-backed operatives over a series of plot attempts in the United Kingdom. Per BBC News, the suspects targeted nearly twenty locations, including a Royal Air Force base in Fairford that houses United States military aircraft. In related security developments, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been relocated to live on a military base due to reported threats from Iran.

On Capitol Hill, the United States House of Representatives blocked a bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. NPR reports that House Republicans successfully derailed the effort, though Democratic lawmakers indicated they may attempt the motion again next year. In separate leadership news, House Republicans selected a close ally of former President Donald Trump to head their minority leadership.

Over in West Africa, Senegal is preparing for a historic sporting milestone as the host of the Youth Olympic Games. Per NPR, breakdancers in the country are fine-tuning their routines ahead of the events later this month, marking the very first time an Olympic competition will take place on the African continent.

Turning to football, the Kansas City Chiefs made a major roster splash ahead of the NFL trade deadline by acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Arrowhead Pride reports that Kansas City sent fourth and fifth-round draft picks in twenty twenty-seven to secure the twenty-five-year-old receiver. To make room on the active roster, the Chiefs waived receiver Nikko Remigio and defensive end Jack Pyburn. Downs led Indianapolis with three hundred fifty-four receiving yards this season, giving quarterback Patrick Mahomes a much-needed playmaker as the team prepares to face the Atlanta Falcons.

On the defensive side of the ball, Kansas City defensive tackle Chris Jones earned his fourth career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. According to team announcements, Jones dominated during Sunday's thirty-five to twelve victory over the New York Jets, recording two sacks, a pass breakup, and a crucial run stop. His resurgence anchored a defensive line effort that held the Jets completely out of the end zone in the second half.

In college basketball, the Kansas Jayhawks delivered a statement victory in Chicago on Tuesday night, crushing the Kentucky Wildcats eighty-nine to sixty-nine in the Champions Classic. Per the Kansas City Star, the Jayhawks put on an offensive clinic with twenty-four team assists, while guard Tyran Stokes helped fuel a commanding performance from start to finish. Kentucky struggled to find any rhythm against the Kansas defense, missing almost every shot from beyond the arc until late in the second half as Kansas coasted to a twenty-point win.

For fantasy football managers, the midseason trade of Josh Downs to Kansas City immediately boosts his long-term value, as he steps into a high-volume target role for Patrick Mahomes. Meanwhile, DraftKings Network highlights rookie running back Kaleb Johnson as a premier waiver target after Minnesota starter Josh Jacobs suffered an injury. Managers should also keep an eye on Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who the team hopes will return to action later in the season. On the injury front, check late-week practice reports for running backs Rhamondre Stevenson and Cam Skattebo before setting your starting lineups for week ten.

Checking your Southern California forecast, Los Angeles is in for a warm and sunny Veterans Day with a high near eighty-six degrees and light northwest winds. Tonight will stay mostly clear as temperatures drop to a low around sixty degrees. Looking ahead to Thursday, expect sunshine with a high near eighty-one degrees and south-southeast winds up to ten miles per hour. An active Air Quality Alert remains in effect for the region. Sunrise was at six twenty-two a.m., and sunset will be at four fifty-one p.m.

In entertainment news, Look Cinemas is expanding its presence in Los Angeles County by taking over the former iPic theater location in Old Pasadena. Variety reports that the upgraded six-screen dine-in venue at One Colorado will officially reopen in December, featuring luxury reclining pod seating and immersive audio just in time for major upcoming holiday film releases.

Comedians Kate Berlant and John Early have been chosen to co-host the forty-second annual Film Independent Spirit Awards. Deadline reports that the long-time creative partners will helm the ceremony on March sixth, twenty twenty-seven, at the Hollywood Palladium. In other award developments, Oscar-winning actress Ellen Burstyn will receive the Performer Tribute at the thirty-sixth annual Gotham Film Awards in New York City on November thirtieth.

On the distribution front, Magnolia Pictures has acquired the United States rights to the animated comedy Jim Queen. According to Deadline, the film premiered at Cannes Midnight and features a voice cast led by Jordan Firstman, Matteo Lane, and Nicole Byer, with a theatrical release scheduled for this summer.

In technology news, Google has officially released Gemini four Carbon to the public following an initial trial with cybersecurity defenders. Per The Verge, Google describes Carbon as its strongest model to date, featuring advanced agent swarm capabilities designed to tackle highly complex tasks. Simultaneously, Google is testing a new, high-speed model internally named Hydrogen and testing an experimental tool called Tabletop that allows users to create customized interactive collaboration hubs.

Anthropic is expanding its footprint in workplace productivity with the launch of Claude Meetings and a broader AI office suite. TechCrunch reports that Claude Meetings can actively participate in work calls by taking notes, drafting actionable project plans, mapping out timelines, and pulling data directly from connected work applications in real time.

OpenAI reported a massive financial milestone, with quarterly revenue crossing ten billion dollars for the first time, up nearly fifty percent from the previous quarter. The company also rolled out verified Business Agents for ChatGPT, enabling brands to build custom conversational tools that interact directly with consumers for comparison shopping and customer support.

Taking a look at weather in Brazil, Rio de Janeiro faces overcast skies today with a high near seventy-nine degrees Fahrenheit and an overnight low around sixty-seven degrees. Winds could gust up to thirty miles per hour, with a twenty percent chance of rain and a high UV index of nine. Sunrise was at five oh two a.m., and sunset will be at six eleven p.m. local time.

Finishing up with Brazilian news, the country's Superior Electoral Court has fined Meta one point three four million dollars. Per reports from the Latin Times, the ruling comes after the social media giant failed to comply with seventeen court orders during the presidential runoff elections.

In coastal Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian Navy safely brought seventy-year-old American sailor Guy deBoer to port on Wednesday morning. Local outlets report that deBoer was rescued sixteen hundred kilometers off the coast after sustaining a head injury during a solo voyage, completing a three-day journey to the Mocangue naval base.

Finally, state authorities in Rio launched a major law enforcement operation targeting a massive fuel tax evasion network. According to G1, investigator officers arrested lawyer Pedro Zuaid, who is accused of operating an investment fund that moved thirty-two billion reals over three years to conceal illicit transactions.

That's the paper.

title: Tuesday, November 10
script:
Good morning, it is Tuesday, November tenth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, expect mostly sunny skies today with a high near seventy-four degrees, though temperatures will fall to around sixty-nine in the afternoon. Winds will be calm from the west-southwest with a six percent chance of rain. Tonight brings partly cloudy skies and a low around forty-nine. Tomorrow on Veterans Day, it will be sunny with a high near seventy-nine, dropping to around seventy-four in the afternoon, accompanied by west winds from zero to ten miles per hour and gusts up to twenty miles per hour. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at six forty a.m. and sunset is at five eleven p.m.

Now, the top headlines. Gasoline prices fell below four dollars a gallon for the first time in three months, though the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high, per NPR. Meanwhile, the average cost for a new vehicle in the United States hit a record high of over fifty-one thousand dollars, with some buyers extending loan terms to finance them. In international news, Russia and Ukraine held nearly four hours of United States-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, though hopes for progress are tempered by past stalemates. In North Korea, the country's spy agency says thirteen-year-old Kim Ju Ae is likely her father's heir apparent. Back in Washington, the House is set to vote on whether to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, while House Republicans prepare to vote on a successor to outgoing leader Mike Johnson following midterm losses. Additionally, the Supreme Court ruled that a federal judge lacked the authority to halt construction on the border wall.

Let's look at football, starting with the Chiefs and the NFL. The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for their upcoming matchup against the Atlanta Falcons following a thirty-five to twelve win over the New York Jets that brings their record to six and two. Head coach Andy Reid addressed injuries on Monday, labeling quarterback Patrick Mahomes with an elbow issue, wide receiver Xavier Worthy with a hamstring issue, and right tackle Jaylon Moore with an ankle issue as day-to-day. Trade rumors continue to swirl ahead of the NFL trade deadline, with analysts viewing the Chiefs as potential suitors for additional wide receiver help. Across the league, trade deadline activity and buzz dominated headlines as teams finalized their rosters for the second half of the season.

Turning to college hoops. Kansas men's basketball is dealing with a significant backcourt blow after guard Melvin Council Junior broke the fifth metatarsal in his foot during practice on Monday. Bill Self announced that Council will undergo surgery and is expected to make a full recovery, with hopes for a return around the start of conference play. The Jayhawks are preparing for tonight's high-profile Champions Classic matchup against Kentucky in Chicago.

For fantasy football managers. If you need waiver wire help ahead of week ten, analysts are highlighting running backs like Audric Estime, Seth McGowan, and Corey Kiner as top targets. At wide receiver and other positions, streaming options and short-term fixes are widely available as managers navigate injuries and bye weeks. Avoid starting kickers like Harrison Butker and Joey Slye this week.

Over in Los Angeles. Today will be sunny with a high near eighty-eight degrees and north-northwest winds around five miles per hour. Tonight stays clear with a low around sixty-three. Tomorrow on Veterans Day, expect sunny skies and a high near eighty-six with light west-northwest winds. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at six twenty-one a.m. and sunset is at four fifty-two p.m.

Moving to Hollywood and screenwriting. Warner Bros is developing a new take on the classic romantic comedy You've Got Mail, with Jason Orley set to direct his own draft based on a screenplay by Deborah. In casting news, Jacob Elordi will star as convicted murderer Gary Gilmore in an adaptation of Norman Mailer's Pulitzer-winning novel The Executioner's Song for Scott Stuber's United Artists. Meanwhile, Millie Bobby Brown will star in and produce the Netflix comedy Non-Refundable, starring opposite Jack Innanen.

In AI and technology. Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, a new tool designed to turn workplace discussions into actionable plans, timelines, and tasks. The company also announced an initial public offering price range of seventy dollars to seventy-eight dollars per share, aiming for a valuation of up to one point four trillion dollars. Google released its new AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, boasting advanced agent swarm capabilities and strong security features for developers.

Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro. Today brings a light drizzle with a high near seventy-four degrees and a low around sixty-six. There is an eighteen percent chance of rain, with wind gusts reaching up to thirty-one miles per hour and a UV index of six. Sunrise is at five oh two a.m. and sunset is at six ten p.m. local time.

Finally, news from Brazil and Rio. Brazil's orange juice inventories surged during the twenty twenty-five to twenty twenty-six season as output climbed while demand fell. Meanwhile, Brazil's central bank signaled a high bar for further interest rate hikes despite ongoing inflation risks, keeping the Selic rate elevated at thirteen point seven five percent. In local Rio news, the Federal Police are looking at shopping malls in the city to open four new passport issuance stations. The city's famous Lagoa Christmas Tree has officially set a date for its seasonal inauguration. And the historic Real Gabinete Portugues in Rio has become the target of an attempted theft currently under active investigation by the Federal Police.

That's the paper.

title: Monday, November 9
script:
Good morning. Today is Monday, November ninth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, it is a mild and calm afternoon across the area. Expect partly sunny skies with a high near seventy-two, with temperatures gently falling to around sixty-six as the afternoon winds down. Winds will stay light and calm. Tonight brings mostly cloudy conditions with a low dropping to around forty-two, and virtually no chance of rain. Tomorrow looks bright and mostly sunny, reaching a high near seventy-five. Sunrise was at six thirty-nine a.m., sunset is at five twelve p.m., and there are no active weather alerts.

Turning to top headlines from around the nation and across the globe.

In London, British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten and a half years in prison following his conviction on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The case was brought forward by six women, capping a dramatic legal downfall for the former Hollywood star who had reinvented himself in recent years as an online political commentator.

On Capitol Hill, Republican Representative Thomas Massie has officially introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Massie is forcing a vote over the launch and continuation of military operations in Iran without congressional authorization, using the maneuver to pressure Donald Trump to remove Hegseth before incoming Democrats take control of the House.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Monday to question the integrity of last week's midterm elections, casting doubt on the results without evidence after previously accepting the Republican losses. At the same time, Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, signaling an aggressive posture toward congressional opposition.

Overseas, European authorities are pointing fingers at Tehran after a major cyber incident. France and the United States suspect Iran orchestrated a cyberattack against European grocery chains, hacking refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and spoiling tons of chilled and frozen food.

Over in the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs got back into the win column and received encouraging news on their franchise quarterback.

Kansas City snapped a two-game skid on Sunday with a thirty-five to twelve victory over the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium, improving to six and two. Running back Kenneth Walker drove the offense with one hundred forty-three yards from scrimmage, while Chris Jones and George Karlaftis led a resurgent pass rush that battered the Jets. The afternoon also featured a major milestone, as Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce officially set the NFL record for the most receiving yards by a quarterback and tight end duo, surpassing nine thousand three hundred sixty career yards.

The biggest scare came when Mahomes took a hard hit to his elbow, but head coach Andy Reid delivered an optimistic update Monday, describing the quarterback as day-to-day and calling the evaluation more positive than negative. Looking ahead, the Chiefs are three and a half point road favorites against the Atlanta Falcons in Week ten. With the league trade deadline arriving Tuesday at three p.m. Arrowhead time, Reid noted general manager Brett Veach is keeping his eyes open, with speculation mounting that Kansas City could pursue wide receiver help. Elsewhere in the AFC, Jacksonville routed Baltimore thirty-three to ten, Cincinnati topped Atlanta thirty-four to seventeen in Madrid, and the conference-leading Buffalo Bills face Minnesota tonight.

On the college hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team is preparing for an early-season rivalry clash against Kentucky.

The matchup features a fresh coaching dynamic, with Mark Pope now leading the Wildcats following John Calipari's exit. Kentucky enters the game looking to regain footing after tumbling completely out of the USA Today coaches poll despite an opening week win. The Jayhawks will look to strike early, while former Kansas standout Darryn Peterson has been turning heads elsewhere after breaking his single-game career scoring high twice in three days.

For fantasy football managers setting lineups and planning waivers for Week ten, several pivotal injury situations demand attention.

Under center, the Seattle Seahawks have ruled out Sam Darnold for Week ten. Head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that backup Drew Lock is expected to start against the Las Vegas Raiders, even as Lock plays through an oblique issue. If you have been relying on Darnold, Lock is a risky fill-in option who could reshape target volume for Seattle's pass catchers.

Elsewhere, fantasy owners should track the Los Angeles Rams receiving room, with updates expected on the statuses of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, while Missouri rookie wideout Luther Burden remains in concussion protocol following a Week nine head injury.

On the waiver wire, Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston is one of the top priority targets on the board. For running back needy teams, Seth McGowan and Corey Kiner represent the week's most compelling additions.

Checking the forecast out west for Los Angeles.

Southern California is seeing another warm and sunny stretch. Expect mostly sunny skies today with an afternoon high reaching eighty-four degrees and light winds out of the west southwest around five miles per hour. Tonight drops down to sixty-two degrees under partly cloudy skies. Tuesday warms up even further, bringing full sunshine and an afternoon peak near eighty-six degrees. The sun rose at six twenty a.m. and sets tonight at four fifty-two p.m.

Moving into Hollywood and screenwriting news, executive shuffles and television development are taking center stage.

Following the Skydance and Warner Brothers merger, Skydance chief executive David Ellison has restructured leadership at DC Studios. Former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham has been named president and chief creative officer, while outgoing co-heads James Gunn and Peter Safran step aside. Gunn shared on social media that he feels incredibly relieved to leave what he called four trying executive years, confirming he is eager to return full-time to screenwriting and directing.

On the pitch front, network procedurals are gaining traction. NBC has bought the pitch for Wild Life, an Alaskan crime drama from Will Trent writer Juliet Lashinsky-Revene following a former NYPD sergeant investigating violent crimes for the National Park Service. Over at ABC, Government Cheese co-creator Aeysha Carr is teaming with actor Ramon Rodriguez to develop an untitled Oakland-set police procedural about a wealthy widow.

In feature news, director Alex Proyas has taken over directing duties on Cortes, the historical epic starring Antonio Banderas that is currently shooting in Europe using artificial intelligence tools. Meanwhile, Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy have signed on to star in Insomniac City, a feature adaptation of the Bill Hayes memoir chronicling his relationship with Oliver Sacks.

In artificial intelligence and tech, a corporate scandal at Nvidia is shaking the semiconductor sector.

Nvidia shares fell five percent after the company board launched an independent investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang. The inquiry follows Huang acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who intelligence officials suspect of operating for China's Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed recently purchased four point eight billion dollars worth of advanced chips, triggering intense regulatory scrutiny that has already led Huang to cancel several major public appearances.

On the model front, Anthropic introduced Claude Fable five point two and Claude Mythos five point two, reporting significant gains in coding, agent orchestration, and scientific problem-solving. Meta also entered the fray, releasing Muse Ember, a lightweight model aimed at executing autonomous software tasks that features a one million token context window at ten cents per million input tokens.

For creative professionals, Medium launched an app called TK that builds artificial intelligence directly into the drafting process, while Adobe and Disney announced a multiyear deal to build proprietary generative tools across Disney's production pipelines.

Heading down to Rio de Janeiro, wet weather is setting in across the city.

Rio is looking at light showers throughout Monday, with temperatures hovering between a daytime high of seventy-two degrees Fahrenheit and an overnight low around sixty-six. Rain chances are locked in at one hundred percent, accompanied by wind gusts reaching twenty-two miles per hour. Sunrise in Rio was at five oh three a.m. local time, and sunset is at six oh nine p.m.

Finally, looking at Brazil, severe weather has created significant infrastructure headaches throughout the Rio metropolitan area.

Heavy downpours have disrupted water distribution across several neighborhoods in Rio and throughout the Baixada Fluminense region. The state government announced Monday it is demanding explanations from utility concessionaires while mobilizing emergency aid to storm-damaged communities.

In regional politics, tensions are escalating over election integrity. Rio's regional electoral court agreed to process a formal complaint filed by Mayor Eduardo Paes accusing Douglas Ruas of electoral fraud, while former governor Anthony Garotinho announced plans to legally challenge the outcome of the state's gubernatorial race.

On the national front, Brazil posted a record trade surplus for the month of October at nine point three two billion dollars, marking its strongest October performance since nineteen eighty-nine. That export milestone comes even as the federal government raised import tariffs on passenger car tires to thirty percent, and as the Philippines enacted a temporary sixty-day restriction on Brazilian pork imports.

That's the paper.

title: Sunday, November 8
script:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, November eighth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, expect partly sunny skies today with an afternoon high near sixty-nine degrees, though temperatures will ease down to around sixty-five as the afternoon wears on. Winds will remain nearly calm, and the rain chance sits at zero percent. Tonight will stay partly cloudy and chilly, with the overnight low dropping down to around thirty-five degrees. Sunrise was at six thirty-eight this morning, and sunset will be at five twelve p.m., with no active weather watches or warnings across the area.

Turning to the top headlines from around the world. In Israel, President Isaac Herzog has officially tapped opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, bypassing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The decision follows last week's election where neither Netanyahu's bloc nor his rivals secured a clear majority, but major parties rallied behind Eisenkot. The former military chief now has twenty-eight days to build a coalition that can control at least sixty-one seats in the one hundred twenty seat parliament.

In Poland, authorities say a gunman who killed six people in Krakow's historic main market square on Saturday held ultranationalistic views. The attacker drove into the tourist hub and opened fire on bystanders before being wounded and captured during a gunfight with police. Investigators later discovered three additional bodies at the suspect's residence, bringing the total death toll tied to the suspect to nine.

In South America, ousted Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has appeared before prosecutors after being removed from office and placed under house arrest on Friday. The Paraguayan Senate voted to impeach Peña following the sudden collapse of a state-affiliated bank, an economic crisis that left millions of citizens unable to access their savings.

Back in Washington, political shockwaves from the midterm elections continue to ripple through the capital. President Donald Trump has offered the post of White House press secretary to UFC boss Dana White, who confirmed he plans to meet with the president on Monday to discuss the role. Meanwhile, exit polling reveals that voters under thirty broke decisively for Democrats, reversing prior Republican gains with younger voters and powering significant Democratic victories nationwide.

In NFL action, the Kansas City Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium this afternoon to host the New York Jets in a crucial Week Nine contest. Kansas City is desperate to right the ship after back-to-back defeats, having fallen twenty to three against Seattle before dropping a twenty-eight to twenty-four heartbreaker to Denver last week. Patrick Mahomes and the offense showed signs of life against the Broncos with three hundred ninety-nine total yards, including a seventy-three-yard touchdown run from rookie Emmett Johnson. Ahead of kickoff, tight end Noah Gray expressed strong confidence in the offensive unit, while the Chiefs shored up their defensive front by elevating tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad. Injury reports are also keeping fans on edge as the team monitors the game-day availability of tight end Travis Kelce, wide receiver Rashee Rice, and defensive back Mansoor Delane.

Across the wider league, coaching hot seats are becoming a major talking point as the season hits its midpoint. Per Arrowhead Pride, fan confidence across several franchises has tumbled, with Tampa Bay's Todd Bowles, Green Bay's Matt LaFleur, and the Chargers' Jim Harbaugh facing heightened pressure to turn their seasons around before the playoff race slips away.

On the college hardwood, the seventeenth-ranked Kansas Jayhawks delivered an emphatic performance, dismantling Middle Tennessee eighty-nine to forty-five. Kansas dominated from the opening tip behind a suffocating defensive clinic that completely shut down the Blue Raiders' offense. Kaufman-Renn led the scoring attack with seventeen points, showcasing the Jayhawks' deep rotation. Head coach Bill Self praised his squad's defensive intensity, noting after the game that holding an opponent to just forty-five points reflects the standard of effort Kansas will need as the non-conference schedule rolls forward.

Shifting over to fantasy football, several major injury developments will force managers to scramble before kickoff today. The biggest blow comes in New York, where wide receiver Garrett Wilson has officially been ruled out against the Chiefs defense, taking a primary target off the board. In Arizona, quarterback Kyler Murray is battling a hamstring injury, clouding his status and mobility for the weekend. On the flip side, rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is scheduled to make his season debut, offering an intriguing lineup gamble. In Detroit, fantasy managers will need to track late pregame reports closely regarding the availability of wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown. Meanwhile, Seattle's Kenneth Walker is projected as the consensus second-best running back play of the week, while Patrick Mahomes enters today ranked as the eighth-best quarterback option.

Checking your Southern California forecast, Los Angeles is in for a warm, bright Sunday. Skies will be sunny throughout the day with an afternoon high reaching eighty-five degrees, accompanied by light north northeast winds around five miles per hour. Tonight will stay mostly clear and mild, with the mercury settling near sixty-one degrees. There is no chance of precipitation on the board today. The sun came up over the basin at six nineteen a.m. and will set at four fifty-three this afternoon, with clear conditions and no active weather alerts.

In entertainment and screenwriting news, international packaging and dealmaking took center stage at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest in Taipei. The Taiwan Creative Content Agency announced it has partnered with private funds to invest one hundred eighty million dollars across twenty-seven upcoming projects. The slate includes an adaptation of the hit series Our Blues, a local stage production of an Off-Broadway musical, and Chunghwa Telecom's new crime drama Gunshot. Additionally, Taiwanese IP outfit Mirror Fiction awarded over fifty thousand dollars in cash prizes to two authors to adapt their published books for the screen.

On the production front, Deadline reports that Crave's smash romantic sports drama Heated Rivalry has secured a rare triple greenlight. The hockey series starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams will simultaneously film both a six-episode second season and a six-episode third season, alongside a companion feature film.

Meanwhile, Directors Guild of America president Christopher Nolan gave an interview emphasizing the guild's fight against artificial intelligence encroachment. Nolan stated that the DGA is actively holding studios accountable to protect copyrighted artistic materials, pointing out that his current production of The Odyssey includes strict contractual boilerplate explicitly barring AI recreations of the production's creative work.

Looking at artificial intelligence and technology, Anthropic is making rapid strides that are raising eyebrows among safety researchers. According to an investigation published by the evaluation organization METR, Anthropic is increasingly deploying its own models to automate internal AI research and development. The report revealed that Anthropic's systems are improving twice as fast as they were just a year ago, sparking debate over how quickly automated model-building could outpace oversight.

At the same time, the broader security landscape is struggling under the weight of automation. In a recent discussion on The Verge, cybersecurity veteran Alex Stamos warned that the multibillion-dollar security sector is being broken wide open by AI-assisted hacking tools that automate complex breaches at scale. Elsewhere, scrutiny is mounting against Nvidia after reports from The New York Times revealed that approved sales of high-end H two hundred AI chips reached an entity in China that operates out of an entirely empty office shell, raising serious questions about vendor vetting and export compliance.

For your Rio de Janeiro weather, expect a wet and overcast Sunday across the Marvelous City. High temperatures will top out near seventy-nine degrees Fahrenheit, dropping to an overnight low around sixty-six. Light showers are expected all day with a one hundred percent probability of rain. Strong wind gusts could reach up to forty-six miles per hour, keeping the UV index suppressed at a minimal rating of one. The sun rose in Rio at five oh three a.m. local time and will dip beneath the horizon at six oh nine p.m.

Finally, covering Brazil and local news out of Rio. The federal government under President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is turning Rio de Janeiro into a national laboratory to test aggressive new public security strategies aimed at dismantling organized crime syndicates and prison-born drug factions. The coordinated push seeks to overhaul intelligence sharing and police tactics directly inside Rio's most heavily contested neighborhoods.

On the corporate front, major Brazilian steelmaker CSN has struck a definitive deal to sell its cement division to China's Huaxin, a transaction that values the business unit at two point three billion dollars. The major divestment comes amid broader economic headwinds, as domestic financial heavyweights Bradesco and XP both trimmed their twenty twenty-seven growth forecasts down to roughly zero point three to zero point four percent, citing persistent inflation above five percent and stubbornly high central bank interest rates.

And in Brazilian soccer, Grêmio punched their ticket to the Copa do Brasil final on Saturday night. Grêmio battled to a hard-fought one to one draw against Atlético Mineiro, securing an aggregate victory of three to one across the two-leg semifinal. They now wait to see whether they will face Palmeiras or Vasco in the championship series.

That's the paper.

title: Saturday, November 7
script:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, November seventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, we have partly sunny skies ahead today with a high near sixty-five degrees and calm winds out of the northeast. Rain chances sit at zero percent through both the day and night. Tonight turns partly cloudy as temperatures dip to a low around thirty-six degrees. The sun rose at six thirty-seven this morning and will set at five thirteen this evening.

Turning to the top headlines around the world. President Donald Trump has chosen Stephen Miller to take over as his chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. The staff shakeup follows sweeping Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections and sets up an aggressive posture heading into clashes with the new Democratic Congress. Trump confirmed on sixty minutes that personnel changes were imminent, hours before making the announcement. Down in South America, Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a sudden banking collapse left millions of citizens unable to access their savings. Pope Leo has begun a twelve-day, three-country tour of South America just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The trip takes him through Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, with the Vatican reporting the pontiff is in good health for his first journey to the region since the operation. In the United States, the incoming class of senators will include several historic firsts, featuring the first Native American woman elected to the chamber, the first Muslim senator, and the chamber's first Paralympian. Meanwhile, counting drags on in Mississippi's razor-thin Senate race between Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom, spotlighting the state's slow and decentralized counting process.

Moving to football, the Kansas City Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium tomorrow to take on the two and six New York Jets. The Chiefs sit at five and two and are trying to snap a frustrating two-game losing streak. Last week, Kansas City controlled most of the game against Denver before a fourth-quarter collapse handed the Broncos a twenty-eight to twenty-four win. Head coach Andy Reid faces second-year Jets coach Aaron Glenn, with Kansas City entering as nine and a half point favorites. The injury report brings trouble on defense. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods is ruled out with a neck injury after missing practice all week, and rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane is also out. Off the field, wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy following numerous lawsuits tied to his twenty twenty-four car crash. For New York, running back Breece Hall is set to return to action, giving the Jets a much-needed boost after dropping three straight games.

On the college hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team rolled to a blowout victory over Middle Tennessee State at Allen Fieldhouse. Kansas entered the night favored by twenty-seven and a half points and put the game away early. Despite the lopsided win, head coach Bill Self noted postgame that he still has real concerns about his squad, pointing specifically to early-season struggles at the free-throw line. Roster adjustments are also in motion, with forward Trey Kaufman-Renn looking to earn a starting role after opening the year coming off the bench. The Jayhawks now turn their attention toward a heavyweight showdown against Kentucky.

Looking at fantasy football heading into Sunday's Week Nine slate, injuries are forcing tough lineup decisions. Running back Cam Skattebo is listed as doubtful, meaning fantasy managers must line up a replacement immediately. On the positive side, Travis Kelce is on track to play for Kansas City against the Jets, keeping him locked into starting tight end slots. For the Detroit Lions, wide receiver Amon-Ra Saint Brown remains on track to play against the Miami Dolphins. If you are weighing flex calls, Breece Hall's return pushes him ahead of Blake Corum, giving Hall clear lead-back volume despite facing Kansas City. In waiver news, running back Dameon Pierce is back on the market after being released by the Philadelphia Eagles with an injury settlement.

Heading out west to Los Angeles, summer-like heat continues for the weekend. Expect sunny skies today with an afternoon high reaching eighty-eight degrees and light north-northwest winds around five miles per hour. The rain chance is zero percent. Tonight stays mostly clear as temperatures drop to an overnight low of sixty-one degrees. Sunrise was at six eighteen this morning, and the sun will go down at four fifty-four this afternoon.

In entertainment news, casting for the next James Bond is heating up. Deadline and Variety report that Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult recently screen-tested for double-oh-seven with director Denis Villeneuve, joining fellow British actors Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor, and Callum Turner as contenders. On television, Netflix has officially ordered a Stranger Things spinoff titled Other Worlds, setting the new series in the nineteen-fifties. Meanwhile, Adam Driver confirmed he will not reprise his role as Adam Sackler in Lena Dunham's five-episode Girls revival, though he wished the production well. Across the sales market ahead of the American Film Market, Idris Elba is set to direct and star in the action-comedy In Laws, with filming scheduled for March in Spain. Rosamund Pike is attached to star in and produce Feed, an upcoming body horror film directed by Leslye Headland. And Korean drama The Remarried Empress set an all-time record for Disney Plus, scoring the streamer's biggest launch ever for a local original after debuting at number one across more than fifty global territories.

In tech and artificial intelligence, funding rounds are hitting historic figures. OpenAI is reportedly finalizing a fresh eleven billion dollar investment round that values the company at one point two five trillion dollars, even as rival Anthropic prepares for an upcoming initial public offering. Product rollouts also continue to pick up speed. Meta announced a new feature called Spaces for its Muse assistant, allowing users to build customized app-style interfaces, like dashboards and planners, using text prompts and connections to outside apps like Google Calendar and Notion. Amazon is rolling out an update letting shoppers text photos or descriptions directly to Alexa to place orders. Meanwhile, geopolitical tension around AI hardware is growing. The New York Times reports Chinese intelligence recruited an executive from Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang. Domestically, Tuesday's midterms showed rising community pushback, with voters approving restrictions on data center construction in forty out of forty-one local ballot measures nationwide.

Down in South America, Rio de Janeiro will see warm weather with a slight chance of rain today. Temperatures will climb to a daytime high near eighty-nine degrees with a nighttime low settling around seventy-two. There is a twenty-five percent chance of light showers, with wind gusts up to twenty miles per hour and a high UV index of nine. The sun rose at five oh four this morning and will set at six oh eight this evening local time.

Finally, turning to news across Brazil, the superior electoral court has officially launched an investigation involving President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin. In Rio de Janeiro, legal proceedings are moving forward in the death of American art dealer Brent Sikkema. A local Rio court scheduled a February twenty twenty-seven trial date for the Cuban national accused of carrying out the killing. Sikkema's ex-husband was recently sentenced to life in prison in federal court in New York for ordering the murder, while the accused hitman's defense claims an informal agreement with federal agents to avoid extradition. On the public safety front, the twenty twenty-six security yearbook ranked the coastal city of Macaé as the safest municipality in the state of Rio de Janeiro. And in sports, the father of superstar forward Neymar has officially taken over as chief executive officer of Brazilian top-flight club Santos.

That's the paper.
